answer.generated: DMA (Direct Memory Access) differs from traditional I/O operations by transferring data directly between I/O modules and memory without the processor's intervention. Unlike conventional I/O where the processor must repeatedly issue read or write commands and manage the exchange, DMA allows the I/O module to take over the memory communication, freeing the processor from the repetitive task. The processor grants the I/O module permission to access memory, enabling efficient bulk data transfers that reduce CPU overhead.
